title: Hiring Employee #1: screen for startup fit, writing, and gut-level partnership
summary: Jason Cohen explains how to make the first startup hire: write a personality-filled job post, filter hundreds of resumes with a free-form writing test, avoid bounty recruiters, and hire constantly by building a company good people seek out. He treats the first hire like a marriage, not an HR exercise.

principles.text: Hire people comfortable with startup chaos, not those who want defined processes and written expectations.
principles.quote: Startups are chaotic, rules change, and there is no "job description." It's better to make a strong decision that turns out wrong, and admit it, than to plan ahead or wait for instructions.

principles.text: Put your personality and culture in the job description so cover letters reveal who fits.
principles.quote: Be funny, reflect your personality, reflect the uniqueness of your company.

principles.text: Bounty recruiters have opposite incentives; they get paid the same however long it takes and push you to settle.
principles.quote: They make *the same amount of money* whether it takes you four days or four months to find that someone.

principles.text: Resumes are only conversation starters; dig deep on an odd detail to test real experience.
principles.quote: Resumes are conversation-starters, but they imply *nothing* about whether the person is right for you.

principles.text: Everyone, even a heads-down programmer, must communicate clearly, so screen with a free-form writing test.
principles.quote: Therefore, some part of the interview process has to include free-form writing.

principles.text: Good hires take 3-6 months, so hire constantly and make your company a place good people seek out.
principles.quote: Your company has to be a place good people will seek, not where you have to go fishing.
